signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + BoJ Hawkish Shift
signals.text: The G10 currency scorecard shows JPY leading the complex with a 1W average of +2.428% across 7 pairs, while NZD lags at -1.516% across 4 pairs, creating a 3.943% bilateral spread. BoJ holds at 1.0%. NZD carries an acute positioning vulnerability with Leveraged Funds net short -32,496 contracts at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range (z -2.60). The RBNZ's cash rate of 2.75% provides a +175bp nominal carry advantage over the BoJ's 1.0% policy rate, but policy momentum is actively compressing cross yield support. Options markets reflect intense downside demand with JPY cross risk reversals skewed heavily into puts. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY, cross-yen unwind dominating high-beta laggards. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep. Risk: BoJ leaves policy rates unchanged without hawkish guidance, stalling the yen advance.

signals.title: USD/JPY — BoJ Rate Hike Speculation + Options Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 155.87, dropping below its SMA200 at 158.44, SMA20 at 159.04, and SMA50 at 160.59 to confirm a clean technical breakdown. BoJ holds at 1.0%. Options markets exhibit aggressive downside protection demand, with the 1-month 25-delta risk reversal at -2.64 put skew alongside a negative vol risk premium where 1M IV at 7.2% sits 3.2 percentage points below 30-day realized volatility of 10.4%. While the Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0% policy differential retains a +275bp USD nominal carry edge (+267bp via SOFR-TONA), positioning remains stretched with JPY Leveraged Funds net short -81,619 contracts at the 9th percentile (z -1.34). Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, policy repricing forcing short covering below key moving averages. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep. Risk: Sustained US labor data strength halts Fed easing expectations and lifts US yields back above 4.80%.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Speculative Long + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7205, maintaining an intact uptrend above its SMA20 (0.7129), SMA50 (0.7035), and SMA200 (0.6985). CFTC positioning data shows Leveraged Funds net long +53,578 contracts, placing speculative length at the 95th percentile of its 52-week distribution (z +1.92). In stark contrast, retail sentiment shows an extreme 89% short bias, creating a clear institutional long versus retail short divergence. The RBA at 4.35% vs Fed at 3.75% maintains a -60bp rate differential favoring the Australian dollar (-70bp on AONIA-SOFR), while domestic Australian inflation expectations running at 4.90% keep real rates negative at -0.55%. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD, trend supported by rate advantage while crowded speculative length caps acceleration. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep. Risk: Broad cross-asset risk-off break pushing AUD/USD back below the SMA20 at 0.7129.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Options Vol Premium + Speculative Crowding
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3526, holding between its SMA20 resistance at 1.3554 and SMA50 support at 1.3449. The options market is pricing an elevated volatility risk premium, with 1-month implied volatility at 11.0% vs 30-day realized volatility of 4.7%, generating a +6.3 percentage point VRP that signals heavy event-risk hedging demand. CFTC speculative positioning reveals Leveraged Funds net long +56,839 contracts at the 96th percentile of the 52-week range (z +1.58), reflecting extreme positioning vulnerability. Meanwhile, UK economic surprise momentum has softened to an ESI reading of -8.7, and the Fed-BoE policy rate spread sits flat at 0bp with both policy rates at 3.75%. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD, downside vulnerability due to extreme spec length and negative economic surprises. Catalyst: BoE meeting 17 Sep. Risk: UK headline data beats trigger a breakout above SMA20 at 1.3554.
